chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Fudayl, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the limit: if a man reaches it, he has reached Hajj. He said: If he arrives at Jam' while the people are in al-Mash'ar before the sunrise, he has reached Hajj and his Umrah is not valid. If he does not arrive at Jam' until the sun rises, then it is a separate Umrah and he has no Hajj. If he wishes, he stays in Mecca, and if he wishes, he returns, and Hajj is incumbent upon him next year.

key_terms.أَدْرَكَ: To reach or attain (the validity of the ritual)
key_terms.جَمع: Jam', a specific station in Mina

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim arrives at Jam' after sunrise during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahar clarifies the critical boundary for the validity of the Wuquf (standing) at Muzdalifah, establishing that arrival before sunrise ensures a valid Hajj, whereas late arrival reduces it to an Umrah. It highlights the Shia juristic view that missing this specific temporal window necessitates a fresh obligation (Hajj al-Mustafad) in the subsequent year, emphasizing the precision required in ritual timing. This ruling underscores the importance of Muzdalifah as a distinct pillar rather than merely a transitional stop, distinguishing it from the Hanafi perspective which often considers it a sunnah.
